```{r project-paths, include=FALSE}
## Repository root: the environment variable PROJECT_DIR, or the working directory.
PROJECT_DIR <- normalizePath(Sys.getenv("PROJECT_DIR", unset = "."), mustWork = TRUE)
if (!file.exists(file.path(PROJECT_DIR, "README.md")))
  stop("PROJECT_DIR does not point at the repository root: ", PROJECT_DIR)

## Values quoted in the dissertation are kept in results/reported_values.tsv
## (columns section, name, value). Writing a name that is already there
## replaces its value, so scripts can be re-run singly and in any order.
VALUES_FILE <- file.path(PROJECT_DIR, "results", "reported_values.tsv")
save_values <- function(section, values) {
  dir.create(dirname(VALUES_FILE), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  tab <- if (file.exists(VALUES_FILE)) {
    read.delim(VALUES_FILE, colClasses = "character", quote = "", comment.char = "")
  } else {
    data.frame(section = character(), name = character(), value = character())
  }
  for (nm in names(values)) {
    v   <- gsub("[\t\r\n]+", " ", paste(as.character(values[[nm]]), collapse = " "))
    tab <- tab[tab$name != nm, , drop = FALSE]
    tab <- rbind(tab, data.frame(section = section, name = nm, value = v))
  }
  tab <- tab[order(tab$section, tab$name), , drop = FALSE]
  write.table(tab, VALUES_FILE, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("%d values written to %s\n", length(values), VALUES_FILE))
}


## Colours
PAL_INK <- c(
  outline    = "#333333",   # bar and Venn outlines
  gridline   = "#DDDDDD",
  annotation = "#666666",   # p-values, n = counts
  threshold  = "#882255",   # significance thresholds, +/-1.96 lines
  fit        = "#4477AA",   # fitted / OLS trend lines
  neutral    = "#BBBBBB",   # non-significant, background sets
  band       = "#EDEDED",   # shaded stage/facet bands and strip backgrounds
  highlight_band = "#4477AA", # tint marking an agreement region (used at low alpha)
  emphasis   = "#CC3311",   # the one highlighted subset in an otherwise neutral plot
## Ink for stars/text on PAL_DIV marks (Fig 4.9): black #000000, worst-case WCAG contrast 4.34 across 21-point ramp sample.
## Not valid for PAL_SEQ (viridis): no single ink stays legible, so labels sit off the dot instead.
## Exception: geom_tile heatmaps use ink_on_seq() (below), keyed on tile lightness, worst-case 4.16 across the ramp.
  on_mark    = "#000000",

  ## Two-tier ink for ink_on_seq(). `on_mark_dark` is #1A1A1A rather
  ## than the #000000 above: on the LIGHT half of viridis both clear the floor
  ## comfortably, and #1A1A1A matches the ink weight of the surrounding axis text,
  ## so the matrix does not look heavier than the panel around it.
  on_mark_dark  = "#1A1A1A",
  on_mark_light = "#FFFFFF"
)

    stop("pal_venn_tgo(): expected an alpha-subunit name (",
         paste(setdiff(names(PAL_SUBUNIT), "Tgo"), collapse = ", "),

PAL_CONTEXT <- c(
  prox_peak    = "#4477AA", # promoter-proximal peak (non-annotated)   blue
  prox_enh     = "#332288", # promoter-proximal enhancer (annotated)   indigo
  distal_enh   = "#DDAA33", # distal enhancer (annotated)  <- KEY CLASS  gold
  distal_unann = "#994455", # distal peak (non-annotated)              maroon
  all_peaks    = "#BBBBBB", # pooled / reference set                   grey
  ## POOLED positional classes, supersets of the four subsets above, used by
  ## figures that split peaks by POSITION only (Ch3 df$Context, Ch4 Subset).
  ## They keep the family reading (cool = proximal, warm = distal) but are
  ## distinct from every subset colour, so a reader cannot carry a
  ## subset-specific claim across to a pooled figure. Chosen by measurement over
  ## the three figures that use them: worst-case dE 34.6.
  prox_all     = "#0077BB", # all promoter-proximal peaks (pooled)      deep blue
  distal_all   = "#EE7733"  # all distal peaks (pooled)                 orange
)

pal_context <- function(keys) {
  stopifnot(all(keys %in% names(PAL_CONTEXT)))
  unname(PAL_CONTEXT[keys])
}

PAL_FEATURE <- c(
  "Promoter (<=1kb)"  = "#332288",  # dark indigo - nearest the TSS (darkest blue)
  "Promoter (1-2kb)"  = "#66CCEE",  # light sky   - still proximal, further out
  "5' UTR"            = "#117733",  # green       - transcript begins
  "Exon"              = "#E69F00",  # amber       - coding body (1st + other)
  "3' UTR"            = "#997700",  # dark gold   - transcript ends
  "1st Intron"        = "#DDCC77",  # sand
  "Other Intron"      = "#EE6677",  # rose
  "Downstream"        = "#CC79A7",  # pink        - past the gene
  "Distal Intergenic" = "#AA3377"   # magenta     - furthest from any gene
)

pal_feature <- function(x) {
  levs <- if (inherits(x, "ggplot")) {
            f <- x$data$Feature
            if (is.factor(f)) levels(f) else unique(as.character(f))
          } else if (is.factor(x)) levels(x) else unique(as.character(x))

  ## Label -> palette key. Which distinctions survive is a deliberate choice:
  ## promoter distance bins are preserved (the text argues about distance from
  ## the TSS), exon classes are merged, and downstream distance bins are merged
  ## (distance past the 3' end carries no claim). Anything not handled here must
  ## error, never be quietly folded into a neighbour.
  key_of <- function(lab) {
    lab <- trimws(lab)
    ## Promoter: keep the bin, but normalise the many spellings ChIPseeker and
    ## its versions emit ("<=1kb", "<1kb", "1-2kb", "2-3kb").
    if (grepl("^Promoter", lab)) {
      q <- sub("^Promoter\\s*", "", lab)
      q <- gsub("[()<= ]", "", q)                    # "(<=1kb)" -> "1kb"
      if (q %in% c("", "1kb", "0-1kb"))  return("Promoter (<=1kb)")
      if (q %in% c("1-2kb", "2kb"))      return("Promoter (1-2kb)")
      return(lab)                                    # unknown bin -> error below
    }
    ## Everything else: drop the distance qualifier, then merge the classes the
    ## palette treats as one.
    lab <- trimws(sub("\\s*\\(.*", "", lab))
    lab <- sub("^(1st|Other) Exon$", "Exon", lab)     # exon classes combined
    lab <- sub("^Exon$",   "Exon",   lab)
    lab <- sub("^Intron$", "Other Intron", lab)
    lab <- sub("^Intergenic$", "Distal Intergenic", lab)
    lab <- sub("^fiveUTR$",  "5' UTR", lab)
    lab <- sub("^threeUTR$", "3' UTR", lab)
    lab
  }
  keys <- vapply(levs, key_of, character(1))
  bad  <- levs[!keys %in% names(PAL_FEATURE)]
  if (length(bad)) {
    stop("pal_feature(): unrecognised annotation level(s): ",
         paste(sQuote(bad), collapse = ", "),
         "\n  Add them to PAL_FEATURE rather than letting ",
         "ggplot fall back to its default scale.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  setNames(unname(PAL_FEATURE[keys]), levs)
}

PAL_SEQ <- function(n = 9) hcl.colors(n, "viridis")

seq_limits <- function(x, domain = NULL, min_span = NULL) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (!length(x)) return(if (is.null(domain)) c(0, 1) else range(domain))
  lo <- min(x); hi <- max(x)
  if (hi > lo) return(c(lo, hi))            # normal case: data-derived, untouched
  if (!is.null(domain)) return(range(domain))   # degenerate: use natural domain
  if (is.null(min_span)) min_span <- if (hi == 0) 1 else abs(hi)
  sort(c(hi, hi + min_span))                # degenerate, no domain: expand upward
}

.seq_args <- function(dots, values, domain) {
  if (is.null(values)) return(dots)
  if (!is.null(dots$limits))
    stop("scale_*_seq(): pass either `values` (guarded limits) or `limits`, not both.",
         call. = FALSE)
  dots$limits <- seq_limits(values, domain = domain)
  if (is.null(dots$oob)) dots$oob <- scales::squish
  dots
}

scale_fill_seq   <- function(..., rev = FALSE, values = NULL, domain = NULL) {
  cols <- PAL_SEQ(9); if (rev) cols <- base::rev(cols)
  args <- .seq_args(list(...), values, domain)
  do.call(ggplot2::scale_fill_gradientn, c(list(colours = cols), args))
}

geom_point_seq <- function(..., stroke_colour = PAL_INK[["outline"]],
                           stroke_width = 0.35) {
  ggplot2::geom_point(..., shape = 21, stroke = stroke_width,
                      colour = stroke_colour)
}

pal_venn_tissue <- function(heterodimer, tissue) {
  stopifnot(heterodimer %in% names(PAL_HETERO))
  i <- match(tolower(tissue), tolower(names(PAL_TISSUE)))
  if (is.na(i)) stop("unknown tissue reference list: ", tissue,
                     " (expected one of ", paste(names(PAL_TISSUE), collapse = ", "), ")")
  unname(c(PAL_HETERO[[heterodimer]], PAL_TISSUE[[i]]))
}

pal_disttotss <- function(x) {
  levs <- if (inherits(x, "ggplot")) {
            f <- x$data$Feature
            if (is.factor(f)) levels(f) else unique(as.character(f))
          } else if (is.factor(x)) levels(x) else unique(as.character(x))
  n <- length(levs)
  if (!n) stop("pal_disttotss(): no distance-bin levels found", call. = FALSE)
  ## PAL_SEQ runs dark -> light, so the first level (nearest TSS) is darkest.
  ## plotDistToTSS reverses its own level order before plotting, so the caller
  ## must apply this to the levels as they appear on the built plot.
  setNames(PAL_SEQ(n), levs)
}


## Bar chart
thesis_text_col <- function(fill) {
  rgb <- grDevices::col2rgb(fill) / 255
  lum <- 0.299 * rgb[1, ] + 0.587 * rgb[2, ] + 0.114 * rgb[3, ]
  ifelse(lum > 0.5, "black", "white")
}

thesis_p_expr <- function(p, digits = 2) {
  if (is.na(p)) return(NA_character_)
  ## The formatted value is QUOTED, so plotmath prints it as formatted rather
  ## than re-formatting it as a number: unquoted, a Fisher p of 1.000 renders
  ## as "1" and 2.10 as "2.1", losing the fixed significant figures that
  ## must be preserved at every mention.
  if (p < 1e-3) {
    parts <- strsplit(formatC(p, format = "e", digits = digits), "e")[[1]]
    sprintf("italic(p)=='%s' %%*%% 10^{%d}", parts[1], as.integer(parts[2]))
  } else {
    ## `digits` governs both branches. "fg" formats to significant digits
    ## rather than decimal places; flag "#" keeps trailing zeros (p = 1
    ## prints 1.0, not 1).
    sprintf("italic(p)=='%s'",
            formatC(signif(p, digits), format = "fg", digits = digits,
                    flag = "#"))
  }
}

thesis_bar <- function(data, x, y, fill = x,
                        value = NULL, value_fmt = "%.1f%%",
                        count = NULL, sig = NULL,
                        facet = NULL, n_lab = NULL, n_lab_size = 3.0,
                        fills = NULL, y_max = NULL, y_lab = NULL,
                        dashed_at = NULL, global_p = NULL, caption_sig = NULL,
                        inside_frac = 0.28, bar_width = 0.62, base_size = 11,
                        title = NULL, facet_free_x = TRUE) {

  d <- as.data.frame(data)
  d$.x <- d[[x]]; d$.y <- d[[y]]; d$.fill <- d[[fill]]

  ## primary value label
  if (!is.null(value)) {
    d$.value <- as.character(d[[value]])
  } else if (!is.na(value_fmt)) {
    d$.value <- sprintf(value_fmt, d$.y)
  } else {
    d$.value <- NA_character_
  }
  d$.count <- if (!is.null(count)) as.character(d[[count]]) else NA_character_
  d$.sig   <- if (!is.null(sig))   as.character(d[[sig]])   else NA_character_

  ## y range + headroom (space for the star that always sits above the bar)
  y_top_data <- max(d$.y, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(y_max)) y_max <- y_top_data * 1.32
  gap  <- 0.045 * y_max            # one label-line height, scaled to axis
  inside_cut <- inside_frac * y_max

  ## fill -> contrast colour for inside text
  if (!is.null(fills)) {
    missing_fill <- setdiff(unique(as.character(d$.fill)), names(fills))
    if (length(missing_fill))
      stop("thesis_bar(): fill level(s) not found in `fills` (would render grey): ",
           paste(sprintf("'%s'", missing_fill), collapse = ", "),
           "\n  Available in `fills`: ",
           paste(sprintf("'%s'", names(fills)), collapse = ", "))
  }
  fill_levels <- if (!is.null(fills)) names(fills) else unique(as.character(d$.fill))
  fill_cols   <- if (!is.null(fills)) fills else scales::hue_pal()(length(fill_levels))
  names(fill_cols) <- fill_levels
  d$.txtcol <- thesis_text_col(fill_cols[as.character(d$.fill)])

  ## ---- per-bar label geometry ------------------------------------------
  d$.inside <- d$.y >= inside_cut
  has_count <- !is.na(d$.count)
  # value line: inside -> just below bar top; above -> primary value uppermost
  d$.val_y   <- ifelse(d$.inside, d$.y - gap,
                       ifelse(has_count, d$.y + 2 * gap, d$.y + gap))
  d$.val_col <- ifelse(d$.inside, d$.txtcol, "black")
  # count line: inside -> below the value; above -> nearer the bar than value
  d$.cnt_y   <- ifelse(d$.inside, d$.y - 2 * gap, d$.y + gap)
  d$.cnt_col <- ifelse(d$.inside, d$.txtcol, "black")
  # significance always above the bar; clears above-bar labels when present
  above_labels <- (!d$.inside) & (has_count | !is.na(d$.value))
  d$.sig_y    <- d$.y + ifelse(above_labels, 3 * gap, gap * 1.4)

  ## ---- build plot -------------------------------------------------------
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = .x, y = .y, fill = .fill)) +
    geom_col(width = bar_width, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4,
             show.legend = FALSE)

  if (!is.null(dashed_at))
    p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = dashed_at, linetype = "dashed",
                        colour = PAL_INK[["neutral"]], linewidth = 0.5)

  ## value label
  if (any(!is.na(d$.value)))
    p <- p + geom_text(aes(y = .val_y, label = .value, colour = .val_col),
                       fontface = "bold", size = 3.5, show.legend = FALSE,
                       na.rm = TRUE)
  ## count label
  if (any(!is.na(d$.count)))
    p <- p + geom_text(aes(y = .cnt_y, label = .count, colour = .cnt_col),
                       size = 3.0, show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)
  ## per-bar significance (above, spaced)
  if (any(!is.na(d$.sig)))
    p <- p + geom_text(aes(y = .sig_y, label = .sig),
                       fontface = "italic", size = 3.4, colour = PAL_INK[["annotation"]],
                       na.rm = TRUE)

  p <- p +
    scale_colour_identity() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fill_cols) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, y_max), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0)))

  ## facets, free_x so each panel shows only its own x categories
  if (!is.null(facet))
    p <- p + facet_wrap(stats::as.formula(paste0("~", facet)), nrow = 1,
                        scales = if (facet_free_x) "free_x" else "fixed")

  ## per-facet n = ... annotation, top-right
  if (!is.null(n_lab)) {
    key <- if (!is.null(facet)) facet else NULL
    nd  <- if (!is.null(key)) d[!duplicated(d[[key]]), ] else d[1, , drop = FALSE]
    nd$.nlab <- as.character(nd[[n_lab]])
    parse_n  <- any(grepl("==|~", nd$.nlab))
    p <- p + geom_text(data = nd,
                       aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = .nlab),
                       hjust = 1.08, vjust = 1.6, size = n_lab_size, colour = PAL_INK[["annotation"]],
                       fontface = "italic", parse = parse_n,
                       inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }

  ## single centred p-value, drawn once (as a plot tag), not per-facet,
  ## so a faceted figure shows one central p-value instead of one per panel.
  plot_tag <- NULL
  if (!is.null(global_p)) plot_tag <- parse(text = thesis_p_expr(global_p))[[1]]

  cap <- caption_sig
  p <- p +
    labs(x = NULL, y = y_lab, title = title, caption = cap, tag = plot_tag) +
    theme_classic(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      ## BOLD: the panel letter is the one bold element of the house style.
      plot.tag          = element_text(size = base_size + 2, face = "bold"),
      plot.tag.position  = c(0.5, 0.86),
      strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = base_size),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6),
      axis.title.y     = element_text(size = base_size - 0.5),
      axis.text.x      = element_text(size = base_size - 2, colour = "black"),
      axis.text.y      = element_text(size = base_size - 2, colour = "black"),
      axis.ticks.x     = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing    = unit(1.0, "cm"),
      plot.caption     = element_text(hjust = 0, size = base_size - 2.5,
                                      colour = PAL_INK[["outline"]]),
      plot.title       = element_text(size = base_size, face = "bold"),
      plot.margin      = margin(8, 10, 8, 8)
    )
  p
}


## UpSet plot
upset_class_cols <- function()
  c("Promoter-containing" = PAL_CONTEXT[["prox_all"]],
    "Genic, non-promoter" = PAL_FEATURE[["1st Intron"]],
    "Intergenic"          = PAL_CONTEXT[["distal_all"]])

upset_bars <- function(a, n_int = 20, base_size = 13) {
  y  <- as.matrix(a@detailGenomicAnnotation); nn <- colnames(y)
  sets <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(y)), function(i) nn[y[i, ]])
  res  <- tibble::tibble(anno = sets)
  res$class <- factor(vapply(sets, function(s) {
    if ("Promoter" %in% s) "Promoter-containing"
    else if (any(c("Intergenic", "distal_intergenic") %in% s)) "Intergenic"
    else "Genic, non-promoter" }, character(1)),
    levels = c("Promoter-containing", "Genic, non-promoter", "Intergenic"))
  ## DISPLAY LABELS. ChIPseeker's detailGenomicAnnotation columns are code
  ## identifiers (fiveUTR, threeUTR, distal_intergenic, lowercase genic). The
  ## text, tables and PAL_FEATURE all use "5' UTR", "3' UTR",
  ## "Distal intergenic". Relabel for DISPLAY only, set membership and every
  ## count come from the untouched column names above, so nothing quantitative
  ## depends on this map.
  feat_labels <- c(genic             = "Genic",
                   Promoter          = "Promoter",
                   Intron            = "Intron",
                   Exon              = "Exon",
                   fiveUTR           = "5\u2032 UTR",
                   threeUTR          = "3\u2032 UTR",
                   Intergenic        = "Intergenic",
                   distal_intergenic = "Distal intergenic",
                   downstream        = "Downstream")
  miss <- setdiff(nn, names(feat_labels))
  if (length(miss))
    stop("upset_bars(): no display label for ChIPseeker column(s) ",
         paste(sQuote(miss), collapse = ", "),
         ". Add them to feat_labels rather than letting the raw name print.",
         call. = FALSE)
  ## scale_x_upset() takes `sets` but has no `labels` argument (checked against
  ## ggupset's formals), so the relabel is applied to the set members in the
  ## data. res$class was already computed from the RAW names above, so the
  ## grouping is unaffected by this rename.
  res$anno <- lapply(res$anno, function(s) unname(feat_labels[s]))

  ggplot2::ggplot(res, ggplot2::aes(x = anno, fill = class)) +
    ggplot2::geom_bar(width = 0.72) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = upset_class_cols(), name = NULL) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.06))) +
    ggupset::scale_x_upset(n_intersections = n_int, order_by = "freq") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Peak count") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none",
          panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
          ## FULL BLACK TEXT. theme_minimal() (like theme_grey()) sets axis.text
          ## to #4D4D4D, a 30% grey. Measured in the rendered png, the y tick
          ## numbers and the genomic-feature names to the left of the dot matrix
          ## came out #3C3C3C-#4B4B4B. Those elements print at ~8.6 pt, so they
          ## need maximum contrast rather than 30% grey. Set explicitly on each
          ## element: axis.text.x/.y do not inherit a colour set only on
          ## axis.text once the child elements are themselves specified.
          axis.text    = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "black"),
          axis.text.x  = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "black"),
          axis.text.y  = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "black"),
          axis.title   = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "black"),
          axis.title.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 13.5, colour = "black",
                                               margin = ggplot2::margin(r = 5)),
          plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 4, r = 2, b = 2, l = 2, unit = "pt"))
}

thesis_upset <- function(a, label, n_int = 20, base_size = 13) {
  upset_bars(a, n_int = n_int, base_size = base_size) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      legend.position      = c(0.74, 0.88),
      legend.justification = c(0, 1),
      legend.background    = ggplot2::element_rect(
                               fill = grDevices::adjustcolor("white", alpha.f = 0.85),
                               colour = NA),
      legend.key.size      = grid::unit(13, "pt"),
      legend.text          = ggplot2::element_text(size = 13, colour = "black"),
      plot.title           = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 16,
                                                   colour = "black", hjust = 0)) +
    ggplot2::labs(title = label)
}
```

## Per-chromosome distribution

```{r, include=TRUE, eval=FALSE, 'Per-chromosome distributions Trh vs Tgo binding (percent per chromosome)'}
# Table 3.1. Per chromosome distribution of Trh and Tgo ChIP-seq peaks (genome version: dm6)

# Ensure seqlevels are identical and ordered
common_seqs <- intersect(seqlevels(Trh_clean), seqlevels(Tgo_clean))
Trh <- keepSeqlevels(Trh_clean, common_seqs, pruning.mode = "coarse")
Tgo <- keepSeqlevels(Tgo_clean, common_seqs, pruning.mode = "coarse")
trh_chr_counts <- table(seqnames(Trh))
tgo_chr_counts <- table(seqnames(Tgo))
trh_chr_percent <- 100 * trh_chr_counts / sum(trh_chr_counts)
tgo_chr_percent <- 100 * tgo_chr_counts / sum(tgo_chr_counts)
chr_distribution <- data.frame(
  chromosome = common_seqs,
  Trh_percent = as.numeric(trh_chr_percent[common_seqs]),
  Tgo_percent = as.numeric(tgo_chr_percent[common_seqs])
); chr_distribution
library(tidyr)
chr_distribution_long <- pivot_longer(
  chr_distribution,
  cols = c(Trh_percent, Tgo_percent),
  names_to = "factor",
  values_to = "percent"
); chr_distribution_long
chr_distribution$Trh_Tgo_ratio <-
  chr_distribution$Trh_percent / chr_distribution$Tgo_percent
```

## Binding around transcription start sites (TSS)

```{bash, include=TRUE, eval=FALSE, "Figure 3.2 will be made using DeepTools and bamCompare in bash"}
# Figure 3.2
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ============================================================
# VISUALISATION PIPELINE, Trh, Tgo ChIP-seq
# TSS enrichment profiles and heatmaps
# Genome: dm6
# Run in the ChIP-seq processing directory: it reads the blacklist-filtered
# BAM files in 07_blacklist/ (not in the repository; see 01_chipseq_processing/).
# ============================================================
set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p 05_visualisation/{bigwigs,matrices,plots}
mkdir -p gene_references
# ============================================================
# STAGE 1, INDEX BAMs
# ============================================================
# Files downloaded from ENCODE (accessions SRR28099027, SRR28099028, SRR28099029,
# SRR28102500, SRR28099453, SRR28099454, SRR28100325) are renamed to sample labels.
for BAM in \
07_blacklist/TGO_rep1.clean.bam \
07_blacklist/TGO_rep2.clean.bam \
07_blacklist/TGO_rep3.clean.bam \
07_blacklist/TGO_control.clean.bam \
07_blacklist/TRH_rep1.clean.bam \
07_blacklist/TRH_rep2.clean.bam \
07_blacklist/TRH_control.clean.bam
do
[ ! -f "${BAM}.bai" ] && samtools index "$BAM"
done
# ============================================================
# STAGE 2, BIGWIG GENERATION
# ============================================================
# --- TGO (paired-end) ---
for REP in 1 2 3
do
bamCompare \
-b1 07_blacklist/TGO_rep${REP}.clean.bam \
-b2 07_blacklist/TGO_control.clean.bam \
-o 05_visualisation/bigwigs/TGO_rep${REP}_over_input.bw \
--binSize 20 \
--normalizeUsing BPM \
--scaleFactorsMethod None \
--smoothLength 60 \
--centerReads \
--skipNAs \
-p 8
done
# --- TRH (single-end) ---
for REP in 1 2
do
bamCompare \
-b1 07_blacklist/TRH_rep${REP}.clean.bam \
-b2 07_blacklist/TRH_control.clean.bam \
-o 05_visualisation/bigwigs/TRH_rep${REP}_over_input.bw \
--binSize 20 \
--normalizeUsing BPM \
--scaleFactorsMethod None \
--smoothLength 60 \
--extendReads 210 \
--skipNAs \
-p 8
done
# ============================================================
# STAGE 3, GENE FILTERING
# ============================================================
echo -e "chr2L\nchr2R\nchr3L\nchr3R\nchrX\nchr4" \
> gene_references/confirmed_chromosomes.txt

awk 'NR==FNR {c[$1]; next} $1 in c' \
gene_references/confirmed_chromosomes.txt \
gene_references/dm6.ensGene.gtf \
> gene_references/filtered.dm6.ensGene.gtf

# ============================================================
# STAGE 4, COMPUTE MATRICES
# ============================================================
computeMatrix reference-point \
--referencePoint TSS \
-b 3000 -a 3000 \
-R gene_references/filtered.dm6.ensGene.gtf \
-S 05_visualisation/bigwigs/TGO_rep1_over_input.bw \
05_visualisation/bigwigs/TGO_rep2_over_input.bw \
05_visualisation/bigwigs/TGO_rep3_over_input.bw \
05_visualisation/bigwigs/TRH_rep1_over_input.bw \
05_visualisation/bigwigs/TRH_rep2_over_input.bw \
--missingDataAsZero \
--skipZeros \
-o 05_visualisation/matrices/matrix_TSS_all_TFs_3kb.gz \
--outFileSortedRegions 05_visualisation/matrices/regions_TSS_all_TFs_3kb.bed \
-p 8

# --- ZOOM MATRIX ---
computeMatrix reference-point \
--referencePoint TSS \
-b 500 -a 500 \
-R gene_references/filtered.dm6.ensGene.gtf \
-S 05_visualisation/bigwigs/TGO_rep1_over_input.bw \
05_visualisation/bigwigs/TGO_rep2_over_input.bw \
05_visualisation/bigwigs/TGO_rep3_over_input.bw \
05_visualisation/bigwigs/TRH_rep1_over_input.bw \
05_visualisation/bigwigs/TRH_rep2_over_input.bw \
--missingDataAsZero \
--skipZeros \
-o 05_visualisation/matrices/matrix_TSS_all_TFs_500bp.gz \
--outFileSortedRegions 05_visualisation/matrices/regions_TSS_all_TFs_500bp.bed \
-p 8

# ============================================================
# Colours mirror PAL_SUBUNIT via colorspace lighten/darken (deepTools cannot source R); use matrix_TSS_all_TFs_{3kb,500bp}.gz (TGOx3+TRHx2) with --colors to match TF colouring elsewhere.
# ============================================================

# ============================================================
# STAGE 5, PROFILE PLOTS (A, B)
# ============================================================

plotProfile \
-m 05_visualisation/matrices/matrix_TSS_all_TFs_3kb.gz \
-o $PROJECT_DIR/results/figures/fig3_3_A.png \
--perGroup \
--samplesLabel \
"Tgo rep1" "Tgo rep2" "Tgo rep3" \
"Trh rep1" "Trh rep2" \
--colors '#DDCC77' '#CCBB64' '#BBAA50' '#117733' '#368C4C' \
--dpi 300

plotProfile \
-m 05_visualisation/matrices/matrix_TSS_all_TFs_500bp.gz \
-o $PROJECT_DIR/results/figures/fig3_3_B.png \
--perGroup \
--samplesLabel \
"Tgo rep1" "Tgo rep2" "Tgo rep3" \
"Trh rep1" "Trh rep2" \
--colors '#DDCC77' '#CCBB64' '#BBAA50' '#117733' '#368C4C' \
--dpi 300

# ============================================================
# STAGE 6, HEATMAP (C)
# ============================================================

plotHeatmap \
-m 05_visualisation/matrices/matrix_TSS_all_TFs_3kb.gz \
-o $PROJECT_DIR/results/figures/fig3_3_C.png \
--samplesLabel \
"Tgo rep1" "Tgo rep2" "Tgo rep3" \
"Trh rep1" "Trh rep2" \
--whatToShow "heatmap and colorbar" \
--colorMap RdBu \
--zMin -1 --zMax 1 \
--sortRegions descend \
--sortUsingSamples 1 \
--heatmapHeight 12 \
--heatmapWidth 3 \
--dpi 300 \
--xAxisLabel "" \
--refPointLabel "TSS"

# ============================================================
# OPTIONAL, PEAK-CENTRED ANALYSIS (RECOMMENDED FOR PAPER)
# ============================================================

computeMatrix reference-point \
--referencePoint center \
-b 2000 -a 2000 \
-R data/final_peaks/TGO_IDR0.05.final.narrowPeak \
data/final_peaks/TRH_IDR0.05.final.narrowPeak \
-S 05_visualisation/bigwigs/TGO_rep1_over_input.bw \
05_visualisation/bigwigs/TGO_rep2_over_input.bw \
05_visualisation/bigwigs/TGO_rep3_over_input.bw \
05_visualisation/bigwigs/TRH_rep1_over_input.bw \
05_visualisation/bigwigs/TRH_rep2_over_input.bw \
-o 05_visualisation/matrices/matrix_peaks.gz \
--outFileSortedRegions 05_visualisation/matrices/regions_peaks_centred.bed \
-p 8

# ============================================================
echo "=== DONE ==="
```

# Defining the Trh/Tgo heterodimer peak set

```{r, include=TRUE, eval=FALSE }
# pintersect(Trh_ChIP_peaks, Tgo_ChIP_peaks) and pintersect(Trh_clean, Tgo_clean) both yield 614 peaks: the two paths are equivalent for the Trh/Tgo intersection.
ovlp <- findOverlaps(Trh_ChIP_peaks, Tgo_ChIP_peaks
, minoverlap = 1, ignore.strand = TRUE); length(ovlp)
joint_peaks <- pintersect( # Joint Trh/Tgo binding regions were defined as the genomic intersections of independently called Trh and Tgo ChIP-seq peaks. Only loci where peaks from both datasets physically overlapped were retained, yielding a conservative set of candidate heterodimer binding regions.
  Trh_ChIP_peaks
[queryHits(ovlp)],
  Tgo_ChIP_peaks
[subjectHits(ovlp)]
); cat("joint_peaks count:", length(joint_peaks), "\n")
mcols(joint_peaks) <- mcols(joint_peaks)[, c("signalValue","qValue")]
```

```{r, include=TRUE, eval=FALSE, 'Figure 3.7b Validating the Trh/Tgo overlap significance using permutation test using peakPermTest'}
# Figure 3.7B
# ---- Dependencies ----
library(regioneR)
# ---- Run the permutation test ----
# pt2_ is loaded by the `load-perm-overlap-trh-tgo` chunk earlier in this Rmd
# ---- Extract components ----
perm_counts  <- pt2_$cntOverlaps$permuted      # numeric vector, length 5000
obs_count    <- pt2_$cntOverlaps$observed       # single integer (614)
pval         <- pt2_$cntOverlaps$pval
zscore       <- pt2_$cntOverlaps$zscore
n_perm       <- length(perm_counts)
# ---- Density of null distribution ----
null_dens <- density(perm_counts, adjust = 1.2)
# 95th percentile of null (Ev_perm0.05 threshold)
ev_perm_95 <- quantile(perm_counts, 0.95)

# ---- Open PNG device ----
png(
  file   = file.path(FIGURES_DIR, "fig3_6_B.png"),
  width  = 3000,
  height = 1200,
  res    = 350
)
# ---- Layout: two panels side by side ----
# Left panel: null distribution zoomed in
# Right panel: observed value alone
# This avoids forcing both onto one compressed axis
layout(matrix(c(1, 2), nrow = 1), widths = c(5.5, 1))
# ---- Panel 1: Null distribution (zoomed) ----
par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, 0.5))
null_xlim <- c(0, max(perm_counts) * 1.4)
plot(
  null_dens$x, null_dens$y,
  type  = "n",
  xlim  = null_xlim,
  ylim  = c(0, max(null_dens$y) * 1.35),
  xlab  = "Count of overlaps (permuted)",
  ylab  = "Density",
  main  = paste0("Null distribution (", formatC(n_perm, big.mark = ""), " permutations)"),
  cex.lab  = 1,
  cex.axis = 1,
  las   = 1
)
# Shade null density
polygon(
  c(null_dens$x, rev(null_dens$x)),
  c(null_dens$y, rep(0, length(null_dens$y))),
  col    = adjustcolor(PAL_INK[["neutral"]], alpha.f = 0.5),
  border = NA
)
lines(null_dens$x, null_dens$y, col = PAL_INK[["outline"]], lwd = 1.5)
# 95th percentile line
abline(v = ev_perm_95, col = PAL_INK[["threshold"]], lwd = 1.5, lty = 2)
text(
  x      = ev_perm_95,
  y      = max(null_dens$y) * 1.25,
  labels = bquote(Ev[perm]^{0.05} == .(round(ev_perm_95))),
  col    = PAL_INK[["threshold"]],
  cex    = 1,
  pos    = 4   # place label to the right of the line
)
# Stats annotation, top-left, not competing with density
legend(
  "topright",
  legend = list(
    bquote(italic(Z) == .(round(zscore, 2))),
    bquote(italic(p) == .(formatC(pval, format = "e", digits = 2))),
    bquote(n[perm] == .(n_perm))
  ),
  bty  = "n",
  cex  = 1
)
# ---- Panel 2: Observed value ----
par(mar = c(4, 0.5, 2, 0))
plot(
  0, 0,
  type = "n",
  xlim = c(0, 1),
  ylim = c(0, 1),
  xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",
  xlab = "", ylab = "",
  main = "Observed",
  bty  = "n",
  cex.main = 0.85
)
# Draw a single vertical bar representing Ev_obs
rect(
  xleft   = 0.3,
  ybottom = 0.05,
  xright  = 0.7,
  ytop    = 0.85,
  col     = PAL_HETERO[["Trh/Tgo"]],
  border  = NA
)
text(
  x      = 0.5,
  y      = 0.93,
  labels = bquote(Ev[obs] == .(obs_count)),
  col    = PAL_HETERO[["Trh/Tgo"]],
  cex    = 1,
  font   = 2
)
while (!is.null(dev.list()))
dev.off()
```

The overlap drawn in the Venn diagram (Figure 3.6) can read 690 while the number of overlapping peaks is 655, because a peak may overlap several peaks of the opposing set; the diagram counts each such configuration once, on the coordinates of the larger merged interval. The two lines below compare the two counts (655 and 690):

```{r,include=TRUE, eval=FALSE}

manual_overlap_of_every_instance <- length(unique(queryHits(findOverlaps(Trh_clean, Tgo_clean)))); manual_overlap_of_every_instance
```

Permutation test for non-random overlap with promoters and enhancers:
```{r, include=TRUE, eval=FALSE, 'Figure 3.7B. Permutation test to show non-random overlap with promoters and enhancers'}
enhancers <- read.table(file.path(REFERENCE_LISTS, "merged_embryo_5-20_enhancers_dm6.bed"), header = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
colnames(enhancers) <- c("seqnames", "start", "end")
enhancers_gr <- GRanges(
  seqnames = enhancers$seqnames,
  ranges   = IRanges(start = enhancers$start, end = enhancers$end)
)
# ============================================================
# Figure 3.7B, Permutation test (RERUN with joint_peaks_filt)
# Uses the same 614-peak filtered set as all downstream analyses
# ============================================================

library(GenomicRanges)
library(regioneR)
library(TxDb.Dmelanogaster.UCSC.dm6.ensGene)

# joint_peaks_filt should already exist (614 peaks, standard chromosomes)
# enhancers_gr should already exist from the enhancer bed file load
# If not, recreate:
standard_chrs <- c("chr2L","chr2R","chr3L","chr3R","chr4","chrX")
joint_peaks_filt <- keepSeqlevels(joint_peaks, standard_chrs, pruning.mode="coarse")
enhancers_filt <- keepSeqlevels(
  enhancers_gr,
  c("chr2L","chr2R","chr3L","chr3R","chr4","chrX"),
  pruning.mode = "coarse"
)

# Quick sanity check
cat("Peaks in analysis set:     ", length(joint_peaks_filt), "\n")
cat("Observed enhancer overlaps:", sum(countOverlaps(
  joint_peaks_filt, enhancers_filt, ignore.strand = TRUE) > 0), "\n")

# --- Promoter / distal split using the same TSS method as Fig 3_11 -----------
# Use 1-bp TSS points (consistent with distanceToTSS already on joint_peaks_filt)
# If $distanceToTSS is already annotated, use it directly:

if (!"distanceToTSS" %in% names(mcols(joint_peaks_filt))) {
  txdb   <- TxDb.Dmelanogaster.UCSC.dm6.ensGene
  txs    <- transcripts(txdb)
  tss_pt <- resize(txs, width = 1, fix = "start")
  ov_tss <- distanceToNearest(joint_peaks_filt, tss_pt)
  joint_peaks_filt$distanceToTSS <- mcols(ov_tss)$distance
}
promoter_peaks <- joint_peaks_filt[joint_peaks_filt$distanceToTSS <= 1000]
distal_peaks   <- joint_peaks_filt[joint_peaks_filt$distanceToTSS >  1000]

cat("Promoter peaks (≤1 kb):", length(promoter_peaks), "\n")
cat("Distal peaks   (>1 kb):", length(distal_peaks),   "\n")

# ============================================================
# Permutation tests - no masks are used, which is the more conservative approach
# ntimes = 5000 throughout; empirical p floor = 1/5001
# ============================================================
options(mc.cores = 1)
# --- All 614 peaks vs enhancers ----------------------------------------------
set.seed(777)
pt0 <- proc.time()
# pt_all is loaded by the `load-perm-enhancers-trh-tgo` chunk earlier in this Rmd
cat("pt_all done:", (proc.time() - pt0)["elapsed"], "sec\n")

# --- Promoter subset vs enhancers --------------------------------------------
set.seed(777)
pt0 <- proc.time()
# pt_promoter is loaded by the `load-perm-enhancers-trh-tgo` chunk earlier in this Rmd
cat("pt_promoter done:", (proc.time() - pt0)["elapsed"], "sec\n")

# --- Distal subset vs enhancers ----------------------------------------------
set.seed(777)
pt0 <- proc.time()
# pt_distal is loaded by the `load-perm-enhancers-trh-tgo` chunk earlier in this Rmd
cat("pt_distal done:", (proc.time() - pt0)["elapsed"], "sec\n")

# ============================================================
# Extract and display results
# ============================================================

extract_perm_stats <- function(perm, label) {
  obs  <- perm$numOverlaps$observed
  perm_vals <- perm$numOverlaps$permuted
  data.frame(
    Context   = label,
    Observed  = obs,
    Null_mean = round(mean(perm_vals), 2),
    Null_SD   = round(sd(perm_vals),   2),
    Z_score   = round((obs - mean(perm_vals)) / sd(perm_vals), 2),
    p_emp     = perm$numOverlaps$pval,
    N_perm    = length(perm_vals),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

perm_results_table <- rbind(
  extract_perm_stats(pt_all,      "All Trh/Tgo peaks (n=614)"),
  extract_perm_stats(pt_promoter, "Promoter-proximal (≤1 kb)"),
  extract_perm_stats(pt_distal,   "Distal (>1 kb)")
)

print(perm_results_table, row.names = FALSE)

# Save results table for export
write.csv(perm_results_table,
          file      = file.path(EXPORT_DIR, "perm_results_table_filt.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE,
          quote     = FALSE)
```

## Construction of a tissue-relevant reference gene set: trh-coexpression dataset

## Nearest-gene context and GO enrichment near Trh/Tgo peaks
```{r, include=TRUE, eval=FALSE, 'Figure 3.10 Venn diagram and Gene Ontology enrichment of TS and SG genes near 614 peaks'}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# FIGURE 3.9, Trh/Tgo peak proximity analysis, hypergeometric & permutation
# Logic: 614 Trh/Tgo peaks -> genes with TSS within 1 kb -> overlap with
#        TS/SG reference list -> statistical tests
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# ---- 0. Libraries ----
library(GenomicRanges)
library(TxDb.Dmelanogaster.UCSC.dm6.ensGene)
library(org.Dm.eg.db)
library(AnnotationDbi)
library(regioneR)
library(VennDiagram)
setwd(file.path(PROJECT_DIR, ""))
txdb          <- TxDb.Dmelanogaster.UCSC.dm6.ensGene
standard_chrs <- c("chr2L","chr2R","chr3L","chr3R","chr4","chrX")

# ---- 1. Filter peaks to standard chromosomes ----
# joint_peaks is the pre-existing 614-peak GRanges object
joint_peaks_filt <- keepSeqlevels(
  joint_peaks,
  standard_chrs,
  pruning.mode = "coarse"
)
stopifnot(length(joint_peaks_filt) == 614)
cat("Peaks after chromosome filtering:", length(joint_peaks_filt), "\n")

# ---- 2. Build single-base TSS coordinates ----
# promoters(upstream=0, downstream=1) gives width-1 ranges exactly at the TSS.
# This avoids the double-window inflation caused by using upstream=1000 as a
# range and then applying a 1 kb distance filter on top of it.

tss_gr <- promoters(
  genes(txdb),
  upstream   = 0,
  downstream = 1
)
tss_gr <- keepSeqlevels(tss_gr, standard_chrs, pruning.mode = "coarse")
tss_gr <- trim(tss_gr)

# Step 1: get all mappings as a list to identify ambiguous Ensembl IDs
flybase_list <- mapIds(
  org.Dm.eg.db,
  keys      = names(tss_gr),
  keytype   = "ENSEMBL",
  column    = "FLYBASE",
  multiVals = "list"
)

# Step 2: identify ambiguous entries (more than one FlyBase ID per Ensembl ID)
ambiguous <- lengths(flybase_list) > 1
cat("Ensembl IDs with ambiguous FlyBase mapping:", sum(ambiguous), "\n")

# Step 3: assign first value for all, then NA-mask the ambiguous ones
flybase_vec <- mapIds(
  org.Dm.eg.db,
  keys      = names(tss_gr),
  keytype   = "ENSEMBL",
  column    = "FLYBASE",
  multiVals = "first"
)
flybase_vec[ambiguous] <- NA   # conservative: treat ambiguous as unmapped

# Step 4: assign to GRanges
tss_gr$flybase <- flybase_vec

# Diagnostic
cat("TSSs with FlyBase ID:   ", sum(!is.na(tss_gr$flybase)), "\n")
cat("TSSs without FlyBase ID:", sum( is.na(tss_gr$flybase)), "\n")

# ---- 3. Load TS/SG reference gene list ----
ts_sg_genes <- unique(na.omit(
  read.csv(file.path(REFERENCE_LISTS, "trh_ts_sg_tissues_reference.csv"),
           stringsAsFactors = FALSE)$genes
))
cat("TS/SG reference genes:", length(ts_sg_genes), "\n")   # expect 2053
#######

# Checks for loss of gene identifiers during mapping between annotation systems
cat("=== Identifier loss check ===\n")
# Step 1: FBgn -> Entrez (used by ChIP-Enrich)
fbgn_to_entrez <- mapIds(org.Dm.eg.db,
  keys = ts_sg_genes, keytype = "FLYBASE",
  column = "ENTREZID", multiVals = "first")
cat("FBgn → Entrez: ", sum(!is.na(fbgn_to_entrez)), 
    "mapped,", sum(is.na(fbgn_to_entrez)), "lost\n")
# Step 2: FBgn -> Ensembl (used by gene length test)
fbgn_to_ensembl <- mapIds(org.Dm.eg.db,
  keys = ts_sg_genes, keytype = "FLYBASE",
  column = "ENSEMBL", multiVals = "first")
cat("FBgn → Ensembl:", sum(!is.na(fbgn_to_ensembl)),
    "mapped,", sum(is.na(fbgn_to_ensembl)), "lost\n")

# Step 3: are the unmapped genes the same across conversions?
lost_to_entrez  <- ts_sg_genes[is.na(fbgn_to_entrez)]
lost_to_ensembl <- ts_sg_genes[is.na(fbgn_to_ensembl)]
cat("Shared unmapped (lost in both):", 
    length(intersect(lost_to_entrez, lost_to_ensembl)), "\n")
cat("Lost only to Entrez:", 
    length(setdiff(lost_to_entrez, lost_to_ensembl)), "\n")
cat("Lost only to Ensembl:", 
    length(setdiff(lost_to_ensembl, lost_to_entrez)), "\n")
######


# ---- 4. Find all genes with a TSS within 1 kb of any Trh/Tgo peak ----
# findOverlaps with maxgap=1000 captures every peak-TSS pair within 1 kb.
# A peak near two genes contributes both genes, this is biologically correct
# for a promoter-proximal transcription factor like Trh/Tgo.
peak_tss_hits <- findOverlaps(
  joint_peaks_filt,
  tss_gr,
  maxgap = 1000L,
  ignore.strand = TRUE
)

# Extract unique FlyBase IDs of all genes near any peak
nearby_flybase <- unique(na.omit(
  tss_gr$flybase[subjectHits(peak_tss_hits)]
))
cat("Unique genes within 1 kb of a peak:", length(nearby_flybase), "\n")

# ---- 5. Overlap with TS/SG reference list ----
overlap_genes <- intersect(nearby_flybase, ts_sg_genes)
cat("Overlap (peak-proximal ∩ TS/SG expressed):", length(overlap_genes), "\n")
print(overlap_genes)

# Save overlap gene list for GO enrichment and the supplementary table
write.csv(
  data.frame(FlyBase_ID = overlap_genes),
  file      = file.path(EXPORT_DIR, "trh_tgo_peaks_vs_ts_sg_overlap_genes.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE,
  quote     = FALSE
)

# ---- 6. Venn diagram ----
png(file.path(FIGURES_DIR, "fig3_10_A_clean.png"),
    width = 1800, height = 1600, res = 400)

VennDiagram::draw.pairwise.venn(
  area1      = length(ts_sg_genes),       # 2053
  area2      = length(nearby_flybase),    # genes near peaks
  cross.area = length(overlap_genes),     # intersection
  category   = c(
    "Genes expressed in tracheal\nsystem and salivary gland",
    paste0("Gene TSSs within\n±1 kb of ",
           length(joint_peaks_filt),
           " Trh/Tgo\nheterodimer peaks")
  ),
  fill    = rev(pal_venn_tissue("Trh/Tgo", "Tracheal+SG")),
  alpha   = rep(PAL_VENN_ALPHA, 2),
  col     = rep(PAL_INK[["outline"]], 2),
  cex     = 1.1,
  cat.cex = 1.1,
  cat.col = rep(PAL_INK[["annotation"]], 2),
  cat.pos = c(-15, 163),
  cat.dist = c(0.06, 0.1),
  margin  = 0.1
)
while (!is.null(dev.list())) dev.off()

# ---- 7. Hypergeometric test ----
# N: all annotated Drosophila genes (background universe)
# A: genes near Trh/Tgo peaks (draws from urn)
# B: TS/SG reference genes (successes in urn)
# k: observed overlap (successes drawn)
N <- length(keys(org.Dm.eg.db, keytype = "FLYBASE"))
A <- length(nearby_flybase)
B <- length(ts_sg_genes)
k <- length(overlap_genes)

p_hyper  <- phyper(k - 1, m = B, n = N - B, k = A, lower.tail = FALSE)
expected <- A * (B / N)
fold_enr <- k / expected

cat(sprintf(
  "\nHypergeometric test\nN=%d  A=%d  B=%d  k=%d\nExpected=%.2f  Fold enrichment=%.2f  p=%.3e\n",
  N, A, B, k, expected, fold_enr, p_hyper
))

# ---- 8. Permutation test ----
# Label each TSS as TS/SG or not, then pass only the TS/SG subset to the
# evaluation function to avoid carrying the full tss_gr through forked workers.
tss_gr$is_ts_sg <- (!is.na(tss_gr$flybase)) & (tss_gr$flybase %in% ts_sg_genes)
tss_ts_sg       <- tss_gr[tss_gr$is_ts_sg == TRUE]
cat("TS/SG TSSs for permutation:", length(tss_ts_sg), "\n")

# Evaluation function:
# counts unique TS/SG genes with a TSS within 1 kb of the (randomised) peaks.
# The ... absorbs per.chromosome and genome passed by permTest internally.
perm_eval <- function(A, B, ..., tss_ts_sg) {
  if (length(tss_ts_sg) == 0L) return(0L)
  hits <- findOverlaps(A, tss_ts_sg, maxgap = 1000L, ignore.strand = TRUE)
  length(unique(subjectHits(hits)))
}

options(mc.cores = 1)   # avoids mclapply serialisation failures
set.seed(777)

# pt (CME perm) is loaded by the `load-perm-cme` chunk earlier in this Rmd

# ---- 9. Permutation results table ----
obs  <- pt$perm_eval$observed
null <- pt$perm_eval$permuted

tbl_perm <- data.frame(
  Context        = "Trh/Tgo peaks within 1 kb of TS/SG TSS",
  Observed       = obs,
  Null_mean      = round(mean(null), 2),
  Null_SD        = round(sd(null),   2),
  Z_score        = round((obs - mean(null)) / sd(null), 3),
  p_empirical    = mean(null >= obs),
  N_permutations = length(null)
)
print(tbl_perm)
# p < 0.0002
```

## Gene-length bias of the tracheal/salivary-gland gene set
```{r, include=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
library(TxDb.Dmelanogaster.UCSC.dm6.ensGene)
gene_lengths <- width(genes(TxDb.Dmelanogaster.UCSC.dm6.ensGene))
ts_sg_ensembl <- mapIds(
  org.Dm.eg.db,
  keys     = ts_sg_genes,
  keytype  = "FLYBASE",
  column   = "ENSEMBL",
  multiVals = "first"
)
ts_sg_ensembl <- na.omit(ts_sg_ensembl)
all_gene_names <- names(genes(TxDb.Dmelanogaster.UCSC.dm6.ensGene))

ts_sg_lengths  <- gene_lengths[all_gene_names %in% ts_sg_ensembl]
other_lengths   <- gene_lengths[!all_gene_names %in% ts_sg_ensembl]

cat("Median TS/SG gene length:  ", median(ts_sg_lengths), "\n")# Median TS/SG gene length:   4685

cat("Median other gene length:  ", median(other_lengths), "\n")# Median other gene length:   1512

wilcox.test(ts_sg_lengths, other_lengths)
# Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction
# data:  ts_sg_lengths and other_lengths
# W = 24279486, p-value < 2.2e-16
# alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0
```
TS/SG genes are significantly longer than background genes, so the hypergeometric p-value is inflated; the enrichment claim therefore rests on ChIP-Enrich, which corrects for locus length.

## Quantitative enrichment near tracheal loci
```{r, include=TRUE, eval=FALSE, 'Table 3.2 Gene length and total locus size adjusted enrichment'}
# ============================================================
# ChIP-Enrich analysis, complete script in execution order
# Section 3.5.4 (main text) + Appendix robustness table
# All uses joint_peaks_filt (614 peaks, standard chromosomes)
# ============================================================
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(chipenrich)
  library(org.Dm.eg.db)
  library(AnnotationDbi)
  library(readr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(GenomicRanges)
  library(stringr)
  library(ggplot2)
})
# ============================================================
# 0. Build peaks_df
# ============================================================
peaks_df <- data.frame(
  chr   = as.character(seqnames(joint_peaks_filt)),
  start = start(joint_peaks_filt),
  end   = end(joint_peaks_filt),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
cat("Peaks in analysis:", nrow(peaks_df), "\n")
# ============================================================
# PART A, MAIN TEXT (Section 3.5.4 + Table 3.2)
# ============================================================
# --- A1. Build custom tracheal geneset ---------------------------------------
all_dm6 <- unique(as.character(keys(org.Dm.eg.db, keytype = "ENTREZID")))
read_fbgn <- function(path) {
  df <- if (grepl("\\.csv$", path, ignore.case = TRUE))
    suppressMessages(readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE))
  else
    suppressMessages(readr::read_tsv(path, show_col_types = FALSE))
  v <- if ("genes" %in% names(df)) df[["genes"]] else df[[1]]
  v <- unique(trimws(as.character(v)))
  v[grepl("^FBgn\\d+$", v)]
}
map_fbgn_to_entrez <- function(fbgn_vec) {
  if (length(fbgn_vec) == 0) return(character(0))
  m <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Dm.eg.db,
                             keys    = fbgn_vec,
                             keytype = "FLYBASE",
                             columns = "ENTREZID")
  m <- dplyr::filter(m, !is.na(ENTREZID)) |> dplyr::distinct(ENTREZID)
  as.character(m$ENTREZID)
}
tracheal_file <- file.path(REFERENCE_LISTS, "trh_ts_sg_tissues_reference.csv")
trach_fbgn    <- read_fbgn(tracheal_file)
trach_entrez  <- map_fbgn_to_entrez(trach_fbgn)
trach_entrez  <- intersect(trach_entrez, all_dm6)
comp_entrez   <- setdiff(all_dm6, trach_entrez)
stopifnot(length(intersect(trach_entrez, comp_entrez)) == 0)
# Print geneset sizes: tracheal genes and complement genes
cat("Tracheal geneset size:", length(trach_entrez), "Entrez IDs\n")
cat("Complement geneset size:", length(comp_entrez), "Entrez IDs\n")
genesets_file <- file.path(EXPORT_DIR, "geneset_tracheal_vs_complement.tsv")
custom_gs <- bind_rows(
  tibble(geneset = "tracheal_custom",        gene_id = trach_entrez),
  tibble(geneset = "All_dm6_minus_tracheal", gene_id = comp_entrez)
)
readr::write_delim(custom_gs, genesets_file, delim = "\t", col_names = FALSE)
# --- A2. PRIMARY ANALYSIS, logistic regression (main text, Table 3.2) -------

# res_custom is loaded by the `load-chipenrich-ch3` chunk earlier in this Rmd

cat("\n===== TABLE 3.2 NUMBERS (main text) =====\n")
print(res_custom[, c("Description", "Odds.Ratio", "P.value", "FDR",
                     "N.Geneset.Peak.Genes")])
# or = 2.27, p = 8.93e-9 for tracheal_custom, reported in Table 3.2
# or = 0.44, p = 8.93e-9 for complement, reported in Table 3.2
# FDR equals the p-value because only 2 terms are tested (BH correction of 2 identical values)

# ============================================================
# PART B, APPENDIX (robustness check, Fisher exact test)
# ============================================================
# --- B1. Fisher exact test (no locus-length correction) ----------------------
# res_custom_fet is loaded by the `load-chipenrich-ch3` chunk earlier in this Rmd
# A warning about locusdef may appear here; the analysis uses a 1kb locus definition
# --- B2. Build Appendix comparison table -------------------------------------
robustness_df <- data.frame(
  Method     = c("ChIP-Enrich (logistic regression, locus-length corrected)",
                 "Fisher exact test (count-based, no locus-length correction)"),
  Odds_Ratio = c(
    res_custom[res_custom$Description == "tracheal_custom", "Odds.Ratio"],
    res_custom_fet[res_custom_fet$Description == "tracheal_custom", "Odds.Ratio"]
  ),
  P_value    = c(
    res_custom[res_custom$Description == "tracheal_custom", "P.value"],
    res_custom_fet[res_custom_fet$Description == "tracheal_custom", "P.value"]
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
robustness_df$Significant <- ifelse(robustness_df$P_value < 0.05, "Yes", "No")

cat("\n===== APPENDIX TABLE: ROBUSTNESS CHECK =====\n")
print(robustness_df, row.names = FALSE)

all_enriched <- all(robustness_df$Odds_Ratio > 1)
all_sig      <- all(robustness_df$P_value < 0.05) 

if (all_enriched & all_sig) {
  cat("\nCONCLUSION: Both methods agree — enrichment is significant and",
      "consistent. Robustness sentence in main text is justified.\n")
} else {
  cat("\nWARNING: Methods disagree. Review before keeping robustness sentence.\n")
}

write.csv(robustness_df,
          file.path(EXPORT_DIR, "chipenrich_robustness_comparison.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
cat("Saved: chipenrich_robustness_comparison.csv\n")
# ============================================================
# PART C, MAIN TEXT (Figure 3.11 dot plots, GO and Reactome enrichment)
# ============================================================
# Shared dot plot function
plot_chipenrich_dotplot <- function(res_sig, title_str, outfile,
                                    dpi = 400,
                                    max_terms = 20,
                                    base_height_per_term = 120,   # was 120
                                    min_height = 900,            # was 900
                                    max_height = 2400,            # was 2400
                                    width = 2400,
                                    fdr_cut = 0.05) {  # FDR cut res_sig was
                                                       # filtered at; sets the
                                                       # colourbar's natural axis
  if (nrow(res_sig) == 0) {
    message("No significant terms for: ", title_str, " — skipping plot")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  res_plot <- head(res_sig, max_terms)
  res_plot$Description <- str_wrap(res_plot$Description, width = 45)  # was 45
  res_plot$Description <- factor(res_plot$Description,
                                 levels = rev(res_plot$Description))
  n_terms   <- nrow(res_plot)
  n_lines   <- sum(vapply(strsplit(as.character(res_plot$Description), "\n"),
                          length, integer(1)))

  few_terms <- n_terms <= 8
  base_size <- if (n_terms <= 8) 11 else if (n_terms <= 15) 10 else 9

  # ---- ADD THESE TWO LINES ----
  legend_pad <- if (few_terms) 350 else 0
  height     <- min(max(n_lines * base_height_per_term, min_height) + legend_pad,
                    max_height)
  
  p <- ggplot(res_plot,
              aes(x = log2(Odds.Ratio), y = Description,
                  fill = FDR, size = N.Geneset.Peak.Genes)) +
    geom_point_seq() +
    # FDR: low end is interesting, rev = FALSE puts dark at low FDR.
    # values/domain fix colourbar range to [0, fdr_cut] (res_sig filtered at FDR < fdr_cut); avoids flat bar when all sig terms share one FDR (GOMF n=1; Reactome n=10, FDR=0.00696).
    # n.breaks = 3, default six tick labels overprint on the 3 cm bar.
    scale_fill_seq(values = res_plot$FDR, domain = c(0, fdr_cut),
                     n.breaks = 3, name = "FDR") +
    scale_size_continuous(name = "Peak-associated genes (n)", range = c(2, 6)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
               colour = PAL_INK[["annotation"]]) +
    scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.8)) +
    labs(x = expression(log[2]~"(Odds ratio)"), y = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = base_size)

  if (few_terms) {
    p <- p +
      theme(plot.title = element_blank(), plot.subtitle = element_blank(),
            plot.margin = margin(t = 12, r = 10, b = 12, l = 8),
            legend.position  = "bottom",
            legend.box       = "horizontal",
            legend.key.height = unit(0.30, "cm"),
            legend.key.width  = unit(0.30, "cm"),
            legend.title = element_text(size = rel(0.8)),
            legend.text  = element_text(size = rel(0.72))) +
      guides(
        colour = guide_colourbar(barwidth = unit(3, "cm"),
                                 barheight = unit(0.35, "cm"),
                                 title.position = "top"),
        size   = guide_legend(nrow = 1, override.aes = list(colour = PAL_INK[["outline"]]),
                              title.position = "top")
      )
  } else {
    p <- p +
      theme(plot.title = element_blank(), plot.subtitle = element_blank(),
            plot.margin = margin(t = 14, r = 8, b = 10, l = 8),
            legend.position = "right",
            legend.key.height = unit(0.35, "cm"),
            legend.key.width  = unit(0.35, "cm"),
            legend.title = element_text(size = rel(0.8)),
            legend.text  = element_text(size = rel(0.75)),
            legend.spacing.y = unit(0.15, "cm")) +
      guides(
        colour = guide_colourbar(barheight = unit(2.5, "cm"),
                                 barwidth  = unit(0.4, "cm")),
        size   = guide_legend(override.aes = list(colour = PAL_INK[["outline"]]))
      )
  }
  png(file.path(FIGURES_DIR, outfile),
      width = width, height = height, res = dpi)
  print(p)
  while (!is.null(dev.list())) dev.off()
  message(sprintf("Saved: %s [%d x %d px @ %d dpi, %d terms, %d label-lines]",
                  outfile, width, height, dpi, n_terms, n_lines))
}
# ---- GO Biological Process -----------------------------------------------
# res_BP is loaded by the `load-chipenrich-ch3` chunk earlier in this Rmd
print(res_sig_BP[, c("Description","Odds.Ratio","P.value","FDR","N.Geneset.Peak.Genes")])
plot_chipenrich_dotplot(res_sig_BP, "GO Biological Process enrichment near Trh/Tgo peaks",

# --- 3. GO Cellular Component -----------------------------------------------
```

# Motif architecture within Trh/Tgo-bound regions

## Definition of regulatory context and CME stratification

```{r, include=TRUE, eval=FALSE, 'regulatory-classification-nearest-TSS'}
# Regulatory annotation
library(GenomicRanges)
library(dplyr)
library(TxDb.Dmelanogaster.UCSC.dm6.ensGene)
txdb <- TxDb.Dmelanogaster.UCSC.dm6.ensGene
# 1-bp TSS points (strand-aware)
txs    <- transcripts(txdb)
tss_pt <- resize(txs, width = 1, fix = "start")
# Distance to nearest TSS *point*
joint_peaks_filt <- keepSeqlevels(
  joint_peaks_filt,   # use the 614-peak object explicitly
  c("chr2L","chr2R","chr3L","chr3R","chr4","chrX"),
  pruning.mode = "coarse"
)
#stopifnot(length(joint_peaks_filt) == 614)
ov_tss <- distanceToNearest(joint_peaks_filt, tss_pt)
joint_peaks_filt$distanceToTSS <- mcols(ov_tss)$distance
# Enhancer overlap
enhancers <- read.table(
  file.path(REFERENCE_LISTS, "merged_embryo_5-20_enhancers_dm6.bed"),
  header = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
colnames(enhancers) <- c("seqnames", "start", "end")
enhancers_gr <- GRanges(
  seqnames = enhancers$seqnames,
  ranges   = IRanges(start = enhancers$start, end = enhancers$end)
)
joint_peaks_filt$overlaps_enhancer <-
  countOverlaps(joint_peaks_filt, enhancers_gr, ignore.strand = TRUE) > 0
# Regulatory class (canonical)
joint_peaks_filt$Regulatory_Class <- case_when(
  joint_peaks_filt$distanceToTSS <= 1000 & joint_peaks_filt$overlaps_enhancer ~
    "Promoter-proximal enhancer (annotated)",
  joint_peaks_filt$distanceToTSS <= 1000 ~
    "Promoter-proximal peak (non-annotated)",
  joint_peaks_filt$distanceToTSS > 1000 & joint_peaks_filt$overlaps_enhancer ~
    "Distal enhancer (annotated)",
  TRUE ~
    "Distal peak (non-annotated)"
)
# Summary table
# dplyr::count() is qualified explicitly because matrixStats::count() can mask
# the dplyr version when a package that Depends on SummarizedExperiment (such as
# DiffBind or chipenrich) is attached; matrixStats is pulled in transitively via
# MatrixGenerics/SummarizedExperiment/DelayedArray. Qualifying the call makes the
# chunk independent of attach order, consistent with dplyr::filter being qualified
# further down this chapter.
summary_df <- as.data.frame(joint_peaks_filt) %>%
  dplyr::count(Regulatory_Class) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Fraction = n / sum(n),
    Percent  = 100 * Fraction
  ); summary_df
## Recode for plotting (same logic as §3.4.1)
bar_df_35 <- summary_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(Regulatory_Class %in% c(
    "Promoter-proximal peak (non-annotated)",
    "Promoter-proximal enhancer (annotated)",
    "Distal enhancer (annotated)",
    "Distal peak (non-annotated)"
  )) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Category = dplyr::recode(
      Regulatory_Class,
      "Promoter-proximal peak (non-annotated)"  = "Promoter (≤1 kb, nearest TSS)",
      "Promoter-proximal enhancer (annotated)"  = "Promoter + enhancer overlap",
      "Distal enhancer (annotated)"             = "Distal enhancer",
      "Distal peak (non-annotated)"             = "Distal peak"
    ),
    Regulatory_Domain = ifelse(
      Category %in% c(
        "Promoter (≤1 kb, nearest TSS)",
        "Promoter + enhancer overlap"
      ),
      "Promoter-proximal",
      "Distal"
    )
  )
#---------------------------- Plotting Figure 3.12 -----------------------------
rc <- table(joint_peaks_filt$Regulatory_Class)
lv311 <- c("Distal enhancer\n(annotated)", "Distal peak\n(non-annotated)",
           "Promoter\n(\u22641 kb, nearest TSS)", "Promoter + enhancer\noverlap")
df311 <- data.frame(
  Context = factor(lv311, levels = lv311),
  Panel   = factor(c("Distal","Distal","Promoter-proximal","Promoter-proximal"),
                   levels = c("Distal","Promoter-proximal")),
  n       = c(as.integer(rc["Distal enhancer (annotated)"]),
              as.integer(rc["Distal peak (non-annotated)"]),
              as.integer(rc["Promoter-proximal peak (non-annotated)"]),
              as.integer(rc["Promoter-proximal enhancer (annotated)"])),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df311$Pct   <- 100 * df311$n / length(joint_peaks_filt)   # denominator = 614
df311$Count <- sprintf("n = %d", df311$n)
fills311 <- pal_context(c("distal_enh","distal_unann","prox_peak","prox_enh"))
names(fills311) <- lv311
p311 <- thesis_bar(df311, x = "Context", y = "Pct", fill = "Context",
                   value_fmt = "%.1f%%", count = "Count", facet = "Panel",
                   fills = fills311, y_max = 78,
                   y_lab = "Percentage of Trh/Tgo peaks (%)")
ggsave(file.path(FIGURES_DIR, "fig3_7.png"), p311,
       width = 8, height = 4.3, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

## Adding CME and Distance to TSS to joint_peaks_filt
```{r, include=TRUE, eval=FALSE, fig-cme-strength, fig.cap="Figure 3.13. Occurrence of the canonical CNS midline element (CME)"}
# fig3_13.png, CME vs Trh/Tgo binding strength (Figure 3.13 in the text)
library(BSgenome.Dmelanogaster.UCSC.dm6)
library(Biostrings)
genome <- BSgenome.Dmelanogaster.UCSC.dm6
# --- Canonical CME definition (E-box ACGTG), scanned on both strands ----------
# CME presence = a match to ACGTG (plus) or its reverse complement CACGT
# (minus) on the FILTERED joint peak set. This is the single canonical CME
# definition used throughout the chapter and by the saveRDS() checkpoint later
# in this file, which recomputes the identical both-strand result.
# The stopifnot() check below checks that scanning is performed on both
# strands, giving 186 CME-positive peaks.
seqs   <- getSeq(genome, joint_peaks_filt)
cme_plus  <- vcountPattern("ACGTG", seqs, fixed = TRUE)
cme_minus <- vcountPattern("CACGT", seqs, fixed = TRUE)   # rev-comp of ACGTG
joint_peaks_filt$CME <- (cme_plus + cme_minus) > 0
stopifnot(length(joint_peaks_filt) == 614L,
          sum(joint_peaks_filt$CME) == 186L)              # both-strand canonical
# CME BED export
cme_peaks    <- joint_peaks_filt[joint_peaks_filt$CME]
no_cme_peaks <- joint_peaks_filt[!joint_peaks_filt$CME]
to_bed <- function(gr){
  df <- as.data.frame(gr)[, c("seqnames","start","end")]
  df$start <- pmax(0, df$start - 1L)  # BED is 0-based
  df
}
write.table(
  to_bed(cme_peaks),
  file.path(EXPORT_DIR, "CME_positive_joint_peaks_filt.bed"),
  sep = "\t", quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE
); length(cme_peaks)
write.table(
  to_bed(no_cme_peaks),
  file.path(EXPORT_DIR, "CME_negative_joint_peaks_filt.bed"),
  sep = "\t", quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE
); length(no_cme_peaks)
#------------------------------#
library(TxDb.Dmelanogaster.UCSC.dm6.ensGene)
library(GenomicFeatures)
txdb <- TxDb.Dmelanogaster.UCSC.dm6.ensGene
# ---- 1. Distance to nearest TSS ----
tss <- promoters(txdb, upstream = 0, downstream = 1)
tss <- keepSeqlevels(tss, 
                     c("chr2L","chr2R","chr3L","chr3R","chr4","chrX"),
                     pruning.mode = "coarse")

dist_hits <- distanceToNearest(joint_peaks_filt, tss, 
                                ignore.strand = TRUE)

# Initialise to NA then fill matched rows
joint_peaks_filt$distanceToTSS <- NA_integer_
joint_peaks_filt$distanceToTSS[queryHits(dist_hits)] <- 
    mcols(dist_hits)$distance

# ---- 2. Enhancer overlap flag ----
# enhancers_filt must exist, with keepSeqlevels applied, before this step is run
joint_peaks_filt$overlaps_enhancer <- 
    countOverlaps(joint_peaks_filt, 
                  enhancers_filt, 
                  ignore.strand = TRUE) > 0
# ---- 3. Sanity check before proceeding ----
table(is.na(joint_peaks_filt$distanceToTSS))  # should be all FALSE
table(joint_peaks_filt$overlaps_enhancer)      # should give TRUE/FALSE counts
#-------------------- CME enrichment by context---------------------------------
df <- as.data.frame(joint_peaks_filt) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Context = case_when(
      distanceToTSS <= 1000 ~ "Promoter",
      overlaps_enhancer     ~ "Distal enhancer (annotated)",
      TRUE                  ~ "Distal peak (non-annotated)"
    ),
    CME = as.factor(CME)
  )
#-----------------Fisher test of 'Promoter vs distal enhancer'------------------
df_pe <- df %>% dplyr::filter(Context %in% c("Promoter","Distal enhancer (annotated)"))
tab_context_cme <- table(df_pe$Context, df_pe$CME)
tab_context_cme
fisher.test(tab_context_cme)
#----------Fisher test of 'Distal enhancer vs distal non-annotated--------------
df_distal <- df %>% dplyr::filter(Context != "Promoter")
tab_distal_cme <- table(
  df_distal$Context == "Distal enhancer (annotated)",
  df_distal$CME
)
tab_distal_cme
fisher.test(tab_distal_cme)
#---------------- Plotting Figure 3.13. CME vs ChIP signal----------------------
png(file = file.path(FIGURES_DIR, "fig3_13.png"),
  width = 1500, height = 1000, res = 300)
library(ggplot2)
pval <- wilcox.test(signalValue ~ CME, data = df)$p.value
p_fmt_12 <- if (pval < 0.001) paste0("italic(p)==", formatC(pval, format = "e", digits = 2)) else paste0("italic(p)==", round(pval, 3))
ggplot(df, aes(x = CME, y = signalValue)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("FALSE" = "CME-negative", "TRUE" = "CME-positive")) +
  ylab("Trh/Tgo ChIP signal (signalValue)") +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x     = 1.5,
    y     = max(df$signalValue, na.rm = TRUE),
    label = p_fmt_12,
    parse = TRUE,
    size  = 5
  ) +
  theme_bw()
while (!is.null(dev.list())) dev.off()
```


```{r, include=TRUE, eval=FALSE, 'Figure 3.14. Promoter vs distal enhancer signal'}
# fig3_15.png, CME-containing Trh/Tgo peaks, distal enrichment (Figure 3.14)
png(file = file.path(FIGURES_DIR, "fig3_15.png"),
  width = 1500, height = 1000, res = 300
)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
df_signal <- df %>%
  dplyr::filter(Context %in% c("Promoter", "Distal enhancer (annotated)"))
## Sample sizes. The labels are named so that each is bound to its class

lev_13 <- c("Promoter", "Distal enhancer (annotated)")
legend_labels <- c(
  "Promoter" = paste0("Promoter (n=", sum(df_signal$Context == "Promoter"), ")"),
  "Distal enhancer (annotated)" = paste0("Distal enhancer (n=", sum(df_signal$Context == "Distal enhancer (annotated)"), ")")
)
stopifnot(setequal(names(legend_labels), unique(df_signal$Context)))
## Statistics
pval <- wilcox.test(signalValue ~ Context, data = df_signal)$p.value
# ---- Live p-value formatting for ggplot annotate() ----
  pval_13 <- wilcox.test(signalValue ~ Context, data = df_signal)$p.value

# Format for parse = TRUE: must be valid R expression syntax
  if (pval_13 < 0.001) {
  parts <- strsplit(formatC(pval_13, format = "e", digits = 2), "e")[[1]]
  p_label_13 <- paste0("italic(p)==",
                       parts[1], " %*% 10^{", as.integer(parts[2]), "}")
} else {

}
ggplot(df_signal, aes(x = signalValue, colour = Context, fill = Context)) +

  ) +

    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black"),
    legend.title = element_blank()
  ) +
  ## p-value annotation
    annotate(

    x      = Inf,
    y      = Inf,
    label  = p_label_13,
    parse  = TRUE,
    hjust  = 1.1,
    vjust  = 1.5,
    size   = 5
  )
while (!is.null(dev.list())) dev.off()
## Class medians: promoter-proximal peaks carry the higher signal.
med_sig <- tapply(df_signal$signalValue, df_signal$Context, median)
stopifnot(med_sig[["Promoter"]] > med_sig[["Distal enhancer (annotated)"]])
save_values("ch3_signal_context", list(
  medSignalPromoter  = formatC(med_sig[["Promoter"]], format = "f", digits = 1),
  medSignalDistalEnh = formatC(med_sig[["Distal enhancer (annotated)"]], format = "f", digits = 1)
))
```

# Hard-masking for STREME (used in Chapter 4)
```{bash, include=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
# DISCOVERY input ONLY (STREME / MEME-ChIP). NOT a FIMO input.
# Mask repeats on the GENOME, then extract peaks, so chrom names match.
cd $PROJECT_DIR
[ -s reference/dm6_hardmasked.fa ] || bedtools maskfasta -fi reference/dm6.fa -bed reference/dm6_repeats.bed -fo reference/dm6_hardmasked.fa -mc N
bedtools getfasta -nameOnly -fi reference/dm6_hardmasked.fa \
  -bed data/chapter3/Trh_Tgo_joint_peaks_filt.bed \
  -fo  data/chapter3/Trh_Tgo_joint_peaks_filt_repeatmasked.fa
n=$(grep -v '^>' data/chapter3/Trh_Tgo_joint_peaks_filt_repeatmasked.fa | tr -cd N | wc -c)
echo "N bases masked: $n"; [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || { echo "ABORT — masking did nothing"; exit 1; }
```


MEME-ChIP was run on meme-suite.org with the settings below (see the Methods chapter).

| Setting | Value | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Tool | MEME-ChIP | Combines MEME, STREME, CentriMo |
| Input | Full 614-peak FASTA | Sufficient n for CentriMo |
| Sequence alphabet | DNA | — |
| Motif discovery | MEME + STREME both enabled | STREME catches lower-frequency motifs |
| Min motif width | 6 | Captures minimal E-box |
| Max motif width | 20 | Covers composite TF sites |
| Number of motifs | 10 | Enough without noise inflation |
| Background model | 0-order Markov from input sequences | Matched to the composition of the input |
| CentriMo | Enabled | Tests central enrichment relative to background |
| Motif databases | JASPAR Insects 2024 + Fly Factor Survey | Most relevant for *Drosophila* |
| FIMO | Enabled | FIMO output is used by the downstream chunks |


The following motifs were rescored with FIMO against all 614 Trh/Tgo
heterodimer peak sequences. The CME was included as a manually specified
reference motif; of the two motifs MEME returned, Motif1 was excluded as a
low-complexity artefact and Motif2 was the sole de novo motif retained.

```
MEME output (memechip_Trh_Tgo_masked/meme_out/meme.xml), verbatim:

  MEME-1  AWWWWWWWWWWWAAHAWATWWAAAAWWWW   width 29  sites 268  E = 4.0e-114  EXCLUDED
  MEME-2  GTRCACTGARARAAA                 width 15  sites  39  E = 1.1e-023  RETAINED (= Motif2)

  Reference motif, manually specified:
  CME     ACGTG                           canonical CNS midline element core
```

```{r motif-fimo-inputs, include=TRUE, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# The FIMO runs use MEME's own PWM files rather than a typed consensus string.
# Motif2's PWM is STRCACTGARARAAA.meme.
# EXPORT_DIR is this chapter's data/chapter3 (set in the setup chunk)
motif2_pwm <- file.path(EXPORT_DIR, "STRCACTGARARAAA.meme")
meme_xml   <- file.path(EXPORT_DIR, "memechip_Trh_Tgo_masked", "meme_out", "meme.xml")
stopifnot(file.exists(motif2_pwm), file.exists(meme_xml))

# Confirm the retained motif is the one the text quotes, so a re-run cannot
# silently pick up a different motif. Read from the MEME header directly, no
# package dependency, so this check works in any session.
hdr <- readLines(motif2_pwm, warn = FALSE)
mline <- grep("^MOTIF ", hdr, value = TRUE)
wline <- grep("w=\\s*[0-9]+", hdr, value = TRUE)[1]
m2_name <- sub("^MOTIF\\s+(\\S+).*", "\\1", mline[1])
m2_w    <- as.integer(sub(".*w=\\s*([0-9]+).*", "\\1", wline))
cat("Motif2 PWM        :", mline[1], "\n")
cat("consensus / width :", m2_name, "/", m2_w, "\n")
stopifnot(identical(m2_name, "STRCACTGARARAAA"), m2_w == 15L)

# Confirm MEME returned this as its second motif.
xml <- readLines(meme_xml, warn = FALSE)
mnames <- regmatches(xml, gregexpr('<motif id="motif_[0-9]+" name="[^"]+"', xml))
mnames <- unlist(mnames)[1:2]
cat("MEME motifs 1-2   :\n"); cat(paste0("  ", mnames, collapse = "\n"), "\n")
stopifnot(any(grepl("GTRCACTGARARAAA", mnames)))
```

## Adding CME to joint_peak_filt
```{r cme-genomic-coordinates,include=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
library(BSgenome.Dmelanogaster.UCSC.dm6)

genome <- BSgenome.Dmelanogaster.UCSC.dm6

# Extract genomic peak sequences
peak_seqs <- getSeq(genome, joint_peaks_filt)

# Search both strands
cme_plus  <- vmatchPattern("ACGTG", peak_seqs)
cme_minus <- vmatchPattern("CACGT", peak_seqs)

# Helper
hits_to_granges <- function(hits, peaks) {

  idx <- rep(seq_along(peaks), elementNROWS(hits))

  GRanges(
    seqnames = seqnames(peaks)[idx],
    ranges = IRanges(
      start = start(peaks)[idx] +
              unlist(start(hits)) - 1,
      width = width(unlist(hits))
    )
  )
}

cme_gr_plus  <- hits_to_granges(cme_plus, joint_peaks_filt)
cme_gr_minus <- hits_to_granges(cme_minus, joint_peaks_filt)

cme_genomic <- c(cme_gr_plus, cme_gr_minus)

# Annotate peaks
joint_peaks_filt$CME <- countOverlaps(
  joint_peaks_filt,
  cme_genomic,
  ignore.strand = TRUE
) > 0

# Verify
table(joint_peaks_filt$CME)
table(joint_peaks_filt$Motif2)

# Peaks with both
peaks_both <- joint_peaks_filt[
  joint_peaks_filt$CME &
  joint_peaks_filt$Motif2
]
length(peaks_both)
saveRDS(joint_peaks_filt, file.path(EXPORT_DIR, "joint_peaks_filt.rds"))
```
